trickyParts: This round's handoff push deliberately carries NO `skip-checks: true` line, though it touches only `.legion/INFRA-575/`. The line exists so GitHub starts no run for a handoff push and the daemon carries the code head's verdict to it (skill://legion-worker/references/skip-checks-trailer.md). Here the code head carries no verdict at all - no run was ever created for de8b7ea3 - so there is nothing to carry, and a trailered push would leave the pull request with no CI for a third round. Retro's push is the rule's own precedent for omitting the line when the head must have checks: 'a base that requires a check will not merge a head whose checks never ran'. The daemon classifies a push by the paths its commits touch and never by the trailer, so this is still a handoff push to it; the only difference is that GitHub now runs the lanes on the head the reviewer reads, which is better than a verdict carried from an ancestor. The architect sanctioned a head without the trailer for this round.

The rule this round breaks for me, so the next role does not repeat it: a push that carries a code commit and a trailered handoff commit TOGETHER gets no run at all, because GitHub reads only the head's message. Push the code first, on its own, and the handoff after it - which is what round 2 did and round 3 did not.
deviations: No `skip-checks: true` on a handoff-only push, for the reason above.
